program_plain: World: a 64x64 lattice of cells (wrap-around edges, 8 neighbours each). Cells have 3 types (type 0 = empty, 5% of cells; random start). Rules each step: an occupied cell whose same-type share among occupied neighbours is below 0.9 moves to a random empty cell.
model_family: Schelling segregation model (lattice gas / agent-based, statistical physics of coarsening and phase separation)
standard_name: Schelling segregation model (random-relocation variant, 3 groups, 5% vacancy, Moore neighbourhood, high homophily threshold)
citations: Schelling 1971, J. Math. Sociology 1:143-186 - original model; seen only as a reference in later papers, not opened
Dall'Asta, Castellano, Marsili 2008, J. Stat. Mech. L07002 - statistical physics of Schelling, coarsening with z=2, two spanning domains below void percolation
Gauvin, Vannimenus, Nadal 2009, Eur. Phys. J. B 70:293-304 (arXiv 0903.4694) - phase diagram: frozen/segregated/mixed vs tolerance and vacancy density; 5% vacancy example with rapid cluster formation
Aging effects in Schelling Segregation model 2022, Sci. Rep. - confirms three-phase picture, dynamical mixed state at high T
Vinkovic & Kirman style unified framework: arXiv 1104.1971 'A unified framework for Schelling's model of segregation' - catalogue of variants incl. vacancy moves
arXiv 2509.14462 'The Varieties of Schelling Model Experience' - blind-relocation agents, persistent stochastic motion at high thresholds
searches: Schelling segregation model phase diagram vacancy density tolerance threshold segregated mixed jammed
Schelling model three types high intolerance threshold domain coarsening single large cluster continued movement
Statistical physics of the Schelling model of segregation Dall'Asta Castellano Marsili
Schelling model unhappy agents move to random vacancy without checking satisfaction, multiple groups, high threshold segregation
notes: Threshold 0.9 with 8 neighbours means any unlike neighbour causes unhappiness; this is beyond the typical studied range (<=0.75) and uses blind random relocation, so the literature on it is thinner. Standard results for 2-type satisfaction-checked models predict a mixed phase at very high T, so the observed clustering depends on the blind-relocation rule. The 'activity rising' label conflicts with g_activity_trend=-5 and is unresolved. The claim that one type fills most of the lattice with 3 equal populations was not found in the literature and may be a metric artefact. Schelling 1971 was not directly verified, only seen as a citation.
full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN, with a caveat about how far the literature covers the extreme threshold of 0.9.**

**1. Model family.** This is the Schelling segregation model, a lattice model from agent-based modelling and statistical physics. It is a two-dimensional lattice gas with vacancies, a Moore (8-cell) neighbourhood and a homophily threshold. The relocation rule is the "random mover" version: unhappy agents jump to a uniformly random vacancy without checking that the new site is satisfying. The three-type, 5%-vacancy case is the standard multi-group extension.

**2. The behaviour and where it is described.**
- **Clustering and domain formation.** Agents with a same-type preference spontaneously form large same-type clusters, which coarsen toward a few macroscopic domains when vacancies are below the void-percolation threshold.
  - Earliest source: Schelling (1971), "Dynamic models of segregation", J. Math. Sociology 1, 143–186. I did not open this paper. I only saw it cited as such in the reference list of a later paper.
  - Physics treatment: Dall'Asta, Castellano & Marsili (2008), "Statistical physics of the Schelling model of segregation", J. Stat. Mech. L07002. It shows static transitions typical of kinetic constrained models, nontrivial coarsening, and percolation-related phenomena. Below the void-percolation transition it finds convergence to a quasi-ordered state with two domains spanning the whole system, and domain length grows as t^(1/z) with z=2.
  - Threshold dependence: Gauvin, Vannimenus & Nadal (2009), "Phase diagram of a Schelling segregation model", Eur. Phys. J. B 70, 293–304. The venue and year come from a citation in another paper. The paper itself reports three phases: frozen, segregated and mixed. It uses 5% vacancies as its example, with rapid formation of large clusters.
- **Review or unifying framework.** Barmpalias, Elwes & Lewis-Pye and Durrett give mathematical treatments. I only saw titles and snippets for these, and I did not open them as primary sources. The best readable framework is "A unified framework for Schelling's model of segregation" (arXiv 1104.1971). It catalogues model variants, including relocation to a vacant site versus swaps.
- **Random relocation specifically.** Every agent with S_i < 1−τ relocates at random into a different vacant location. A teaching note says that, for sufficiently low tolerance or low vacancy rate, no static equilibrium exists. This is the "no frozen state, activity persists" regime.
- **Multi-type version.** Three or more groups is a routine extension, and the same clustering and coarsening are expected. I found no dedicated three-type paper in my searches.

**3. Differences from the canonical literature, and whether they matter.**
- **Extreme threshold.** At a threshold of 0.9 with 8 neighbours, any single unlike neighbour makes an agent unhappy, since 7/8 = 0.875 < 0.9. That is far above the usual 0.3–0.75 range studied.
  - For two types with satisfaction-checked moves, Gauvin et al. and the aging paper (a dynamical disordered (mixed) state at high tolerance, with small clusters continually created and annihilated) predict a mixed phase at very high T.
  - Your blind-relocation rule is different. A mover can land on an unsatisfying site, so the system never freezes.
  - A related blind-relocation study (arXiv 2509.14462) says stochastic motion persists when few agents find satisfactory sites. I did not find a paper that reports your exact setting, which is threshold 0.9, three types, 5% vacancy and blind relocation.
- **Activity "rising".** Your log shows g_activity_trend = −5 but labels it "activity rising", which may be a sign or labelling issue. Persistent activity is expected, because interface agents are always unhappy at this threshold. I can't say whether it should rise or fall without seeing the time series. Declining activity as clusters coarsen is what the standard picture predicts.
- **One type filling most of the lattice.** This is a stronger claim than "a few domains". It is plausible as a result of coarsening, but with three equal populations it would mean one type absorbing the others' space. That is not part of the standard picture, where domain sizes tend to stay comparable. I found no literature on it. It may be a metric artefact, such as the largest connected component of one type, or a finite-size or transient effect.

**4. Confidence: medium.**
- **High confidence** that the Schelling model with random relocation shows clustering (high Moran's I) and coarsening, and that the 0.85 and 0.9 variants belong to the same class. Multiple independent sources cover this.
- **Lower confidence** on the threshold-0.9 and dominant-single-domain details. The literature I could read covers mostly two types and thresholds up to about 0.75, and I did not verify the blind-relocation extreme.
- The "activity rising" label is unresolved.

Searches run:
1. Schelling phase diagram, vacancy and tolerance
2. Schelling three types, high intolerance, coarsening
3. Dall'Asta, Castellano & Marsili
4. Schelling blind random relocation with multiple groups
